scene.requestPrompt: A Lisbon neighborhood tasca with tiled walls, chalkboard menu, worn wood counter, small plates, bottles, and the clutter of an everyday lunch rush.
scene.title: Lisbon Tasca Interior
scene.blurb: A traditional Lisbon neighborhood tasca featuring iconic azulejo tiled walls, a worn wooden counter, and the vibrant clutter of a busy lunchtime rush.
scene.summary: This diorama depicts a small, bustling tasca—a casual Portuguese tavern—characterized by its distinctive blue and white azulejo tile walls, a well-worn wood counter with visible patina, chalkboard menus displaying petiscos (small plates), and bottles of locally produced wines and spirits. The interior captures the dense everyday atmosphere with layered utensils, glassware, Portuguese ceramics, linens, and glimpses of community life through informal seating arrangements and wall-mounted details.

details.title: Azulejo Tiled Walls
details.body: The blue and white azulejo ceramic tiles are iconic of Portuguese culture and architecture, particularly in Lisbon. They adorn the tavern walls creating a cool tactile backdrop that resists kitchen humidity, while expressing historic artistry and everyday beauty.

details.title: Chalkboard Menu
details.body: Handwritten chalkboard menu boards present the day's petiscos and wine offerings in Portuguese, emphasizing neighborhood charm and flexibility to update specials frequently. The hand lettering adds to the convivial atmosphere.

details.title: Worn Wooden Counter
details.body: The well-used wooden counter has a rich patina, with softened edges and tiny dents from years of service. This natural wear tells stories about the tasca's history and adds warmth and texture to the interior space.

details.title: Portuguese Small Plates (Petiscos)
details.body: Small plates with remnants of olives, salted cod, chorizo, and other petiscos reflect common sharing culture at tascas, promoting social dining with a variety of flavors and textures.

details.title: Glass Bottles and Ceramics
details.body: Locally produced wine bottles and hand-painted ceramic vessels contrast with glassware and contribute to authentic visual clutter, embodying Portuguese viniculture and artisanal traditions.
